SECTION 1 — IDENTITY AND TASK

You are performing a pre-ship security and correctness audit on a Python patch for a paper trading bot (alpaca-mtf-both). Your role: find what the internal team missed. Be concrete and technical — no hedging.

SECTION 2 — FILE CONTEXT

File: scan_to_html.py (2358 lines)
RTH-chain: YES — run_cycle.py imports write_scan_html() from this file and calls it during regular trading hours
Role: Scores the 25-ticker watchlist, builds scan_results.html for the operator UI, and is called every 5-min scan cycle

SECTION 3 — THE BUG (exact failure scenario)

Function: avg_volume() at lines 208-213 (original)
Bug: When all volume values in the rolling 20-bar window are NaN (common on fresh/thin tickers), pandas .mean() returns float('nan'). Python's float(NaN) succeeds silently — NaN is returned instead of None.

Caller path (scan_ticker, lines 314-318):
    av = avg_volume(daily)
    if av:  # BUG: NaN is truthy in Python — this passes for NaN
        r["avg_vol"] = av
        today_vol = float(daily["volume"].iloc[-1])
        r["vol_ratio"] = round(today_vol / av, 2)  # NaN stored in vol_ratio

The NaN propagates downstream. In write_scan_html's HTML formatting pipeline, an int() conversion is called on the NaN value:
    int(float('nan'))  → ValueError: cannot convert float NaN to integer

This crashed write_scan_html 10 times across 10 consecutive scan cycles (confirmed in logs). The crash is caught by write_scan_html's outer except and logged as WARNING — the bot continues running but the scan HTML is not written for that cycle.

SECTION 4 — THE PROPOSED FIX (exact diff)

--- scan_to_html.py (original)
+++ scan_to_html.py (proposed)

     try:
-        return float(daily_df["volume"].tail(period).mean())
+        result = daily_df["volume"].tail(period).mean()
+        if result != result:  # NaN != NaN is always True; guards all-NaN volume series
+            logger.debug("avg_volume: all-NaN volume series — returning None")
+            return None
+        return float(result)
     except Exception as _vol_e:
         logger.debug("avg_volume: computation failed — %s", _vol_e)
         return None
